question: Mahesh bought some pens at the rate of ₹180 a dozen. He sold them for ₹19 each. His profit percentage is ______. (Round off your answer to two decimal places.)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cost Price of 1 pen = 180 ÷ 12 = ₹15

Profit per pen = SP − CP = 19 − 15 = ₹4

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 = (4 ÷ 15) × 100 ≈ 26.67%

**∴ The correct answer is 26.67%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price of 1 dozen (12) pens = ₹180

Selling Price of 1 pen = ₹19

**Formula Used:**

Profit = Selling Price (SP) − Cost Price (CP)

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 CP = ₹15
 
 
 SP = ₹19

 
• 
 Profit = ₹4

 Profit % = (4 ÷ 15) × 100 ≈ 26.67%

**Calculation:**

⇒ Cost Price (CP) of 1 pen = 180 ÷ 12 = ₹15

⇒ Selling Price (SP) of 1 pen = ₹19

⇒ Profit = 19 − 15 = ₹4

⇒ Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (4 ÷ 15) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 400 ÷ 15 = 80 ÷ 3

⇒ Profit % = 26.666... % ≈ 26.67%

**∴ The correct answer is 26.67%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit & Loss Percentage

Profit or loss percentage is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless stated otherwise. Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). SP = MP − Discount.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, then Net Discount = a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100.
